outcome: Risk factors for prenatal depressive symptoms
cohort: 2305 pregnant and postpartum women (18-48 years old) registered in the Babol Pregnancy Mental Health Registry (BPMHR) database from June 2020 to March 2021.
finding: The prevalence of depressive symptoms was higher in pregnant women (19.8%) than in postpartum women (11.6%), and risk factors for prenatal depressive symptoms included high parity, gestational age in the first or second trimester, and high-risk pregnancy.
